verdict: ESCALATE - two independent mandatory triggers fire. First, the benches are discordant on the core case: red recommends REJECT-as-a-starter and FLAT into end-November, blue rules PARTIALLY OVERTURNED and lands on a half-starter, staged. Second, that surviving outcome is a BUY, and any buy outcome escalates by rule. Red's conviction of 6 is also the weakest full-court score in this batch, and red says so honestly - it explicitly declines to call any finding FATAL because approvability cannot be refuted, so the kill rests on edge-unverifiability plus informed supply rather than on a broken fact. The substance. The screen hit is a measurement artifact and the triage said so first: on 2025-09-29 MLTX fell about 90% in one session, from $61.99 to $6.24, when VELA-2's Week-16 primary missed under the composite estimand (delta 9%, p=0.053) while VELA-1 hit (delta 17%, p<0.001). The 52-week high is a pre-event price from a dead information regime, so dd52 of -0.709 measures the gap, not a dislocation - in the current regime the stock is up 178% off its $5.95 low and 25% below its 26-week high. What makes it court-worthy anyway is that the regulatory leg has been de-risked while the price still discounts a failed drug: the final pre-BLA meeting was positive, the FDA accepted the Phase 2 MIRA study as substantial evidence of effectiveness plus the adolescent data, with no remaining gaps precluding the planned submission, and the BLA is due end-September 2026. On the identical Week-16 HiSCR75 endpoint at similar placebo rates, VELA-1 delivered 35.4% versus 21.6% placebo (about 17pp) against Bimzelx's 33.4% versus 18.4% (about 15pp), and Week-52 durability is 67.2% versus Bimzelx's over-55% at Week 48. Red resolved the triage's open question about that comparison in the thesis's favor - the 67.2% is as-observed, n=396, the same basis as Bimzelx's observed-case figure - then argued both are survivorship-inflated off roughly 840 randomized, so it is not differentiation evidence. Blue correctly graded that a REDUCTION rather than a confirmation: like-for-like on the same basis is weak-but-directional support, and calling it 'not evidence' overstates. The decisive disagreement is about IZAR-1, the positive Phase 3 in psoriatic arthritis announced 2026-08-10, after which the stock fell 6.3% and then a further 5.3%. Red's strongest kill is that the company announced a pivotal win disclosing only absolute rates (ACR50 42.1%, ACR20 66.5%, PASI90 61%) while comparative analyses versus placebo remain blinded to Week 52, with full readout in H1 2027 per CT.gov NCT06641076 - so the one variable that decides the case, differentiation, is structurally unobservable for six to nine months, and in exactly that fog the CEO, CSO and CFO distributed about $5M at roughly $20 in July and the company filed an S-3ASR the same day as its own positive print. Blue overturned the core of that on a bound red never computed. 'Met all endpoints' plus a title claiming significant improvements means significance versus placebo is asserted at topline, so a VELA-2-style significance miss is already off the table - the hidden variable is MAGNITUDE only. And magnitude is bounded: BE OPTIMAL's bio-naive placebo ACR50 was 10% (28/281), and PsA placebo ACR50 rates are stable at 10-15%, unlike the volatile HS HiSCR placebo that actually killed VELA-2. A 42.1% absolute therefore implies a delta near 30pp - parity with Bimzelx. Red treated PsA like HS; that is the decisive omission and blue named it as such. Blue also reduced red's shelf finding: an S-3ASR filed the same day as the 10-Q is routine WKSI mechanics and the S-8 is plan housekeeping, so 'management armed a raise while holding the delta' reads intent into calendar mechanics - supply before launch stays near-certain on runway math ($537.0M cash against $61.6M quarterly opex, about 8.7 quarters only at flat opex, and a commercial build breaks that), but the timing is not a tell. Blue sustained the insider distribution as a sizing cap rather than a signal (10b5-1 plans adopted March 2026, post-crash, executed 20% above the current tape), sustained that approvability rests on the issuer's paraphrase of a private FDA meeting with no public FDA text - correctly PLAUSIBLE-only on both benches - and sustained the EV as an upper bound because the Hercules drawn balance is unverifiable behind a persistent EDGAR 403. Where I land pending escalation: blue's placebo-floor bound is the better argument and red's FLAT ignores two dated, company-guided, buyer-favorable events inside its own window - the BLA submission around 9/30 and the filing-acceptance plus priority-review determination around end-November - against a price 18% below where a $230M institutional book cleared in June. But the case for a position is a half-starter at most, and the escalation must set size against three live tails the court did not close: an unverifiable Hercules balance, an unread 10-Q, and a differentiation number the company possesses and will not show until H1 2027. One correction the escalation must carry into any write-up: end-November is the 60-day filing-acceptance and priority-review determination, NOT a PDUFA decision - a secondary summary called it a PDUFA date and that is wrong. PDUFA lands around March 2027 on priority review or July 2027 on standard, with guided launch in 2H27. || SESSION RULING: ESCALATION RULED: half-starter RATIFIED as blue drafted, with two hard preconditions BEFORE any order: (1) Hercules facility balance read from primary (now closable via sec_fetch/proxy path); (2) sizing per catalyst-options doctrine — this is a binary (BLA ~9/30, acceptance ~11/30, PDUFA ~Mar-27 priority — NOT Nov, the secondary-source error the draft caught); equity half-starter only, no options, defined loss = position size. (2) EV was BACKWARDS: ~$985M not $845M-upper-bound (omitted $100M drawn Hercules + pre-funded warrants). (3) Committed drawable capacity = $0: Tranche 4 ($50M) is ARITHMETICALLY DEAD (needs 10 consecutive closes >=$17.62 before 8/20; 6 of last 11 fail); T6 $200M is lender-discretionary. The 8/10 PR's 'up to $400M non-dilutive remains available' = marketed-takeaway divergence (datum disclosed same day in the 10-Q) — review-flag not fraud. (4) Blue's placebo floor INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED (9 registrational trials, 4 sponsors: 7.1-15.1%, SD 2.6pp) — but the bound proves the drug WORKS, not that it's DIFFERENTIATED: 42.1% vs approved bimekizumab's 43.9% same endpoint/week, parity the CEO volunteers. (5) ATTRIBUTION ERROR in my own ruling: the BLA is HS (VELA/MIRA); the PsA readout (IZAR-1) doesn't touch the dated catalyst. (6) Issuer is CLEAN — endpoint hierarchy intact, NCT binding clean, honest disclosure throughout; the errors were the court's, not the company's. Fair-value option on an HS approval, equity-financed (ATM live 17% below the June clear), NOT a cheap option on a differentiated asset.
